v1_2_5.title: The Global Language Update
v1_2_5.desc: Breaking language barriers, PODS is now multilingual. We implemented a robust internationalization (i18n) engine with support for Portuguese, English, and Simplified Chinese. User preferences are now persistent across sessions, stored directly in your Firestore profile.

v1_2_0.desc: This version transforms the PODS Admin into a living ecosystem. We replaced static placeholders with real-time Firestore data streams, introduced a Global Notification Center, and launched the collective task system 'Fast Track'.
changes: Global Notification Center with Deep Links
Automated System Logs and Audit Trails
User Assignment and Push Alerts in Kanban

Streetlight.title: Streetlight - Testbook
Streetlight.subtitle: Exploring Streetlight: A Complete Guide for PODS Administrators

1_1.title: 1.1 Document Structure
1_1.p1: Each test presented here includes: precondition (minimum conditions for the test to occur), execution (numbered steps to perform the tests), and postcondition (expected result).
1_1.p2: Some tests will also include tip or error annotations according to the standards below:

alertTip.title: Tip
alertTip.content: This marker indicates tips when performing a test.

alertWarning.title: Warning
alertWarning.content: This marker indicates points of attention regarding the test or expected result.

alertError.title: Error
alertError.content: This marker indicates issues in the documentation.

1_2.title: 1.2 About the Tests
1_2.p1: The tests described here are performed through the MDC graphical interface, known as ORCA. All tests also assume the existence of:
items: An AP (Access Point/Gateway).
A luminaire with a smart controller.
(Optional) Smart energy meters.

2_1.title: 2.1 Network Management System
2_1.p1: The Network Management System menu is used to register, configure, and manage network devices. This page will provide all necessary guidance for registering, monitoring, and maintaining network devices. To access this menu, click Network Management in the sidebar.

precondition.title: Precondition
precondition.content: Access to the Streetlight system with valid credentials.

2_1_1.title: 2.1.1 Dashboard
2_1_1.p1: The Dashboard is the quickest way to analyze network behavior. It provides information about:
items: Number of devices online;
Device communication quality;
LastGasp alarms.
2_1_1.instruction: To access the Dashboard, select Network Management > Dashboard from the sidebar. The following page will be displayed:

2_1_2.title: 2.1.2 Quality Measurement
2_1_2.p1: Below is a brief explanation of each quality measurement:
2_1_2.rssiContent: Measurement of the power present in a received radio signal. It is useful for determining whether the signal is sufficient for a good wireless connection. Devices with a measured parameter above -90dBm are classified in a satisfactory power category.
2_1_2.lqiContent: Indication of the quality of data packets received by the receiver. Devices with an indicator above 85 are classified in a satisfactory quality category.

2_2_1_network.title: 2.2.1 Network
2_2_1_network.p1: The Network page is used to monitor the communication of each Gateway individually, providing a graphical view of the current topology and devices connected to a specific Gateway.
2_2_1_network.p2: The search condition for the Network page functionality is simple and uses only the Gateway ID as a criterion. After selecting the Gateway, click the CALL button for a real-time topology view, or LOADING for a more detailed view of the last topology collected by the system.

warningCall.title: Warning
warningCall.content: To avoid overloading the network, the CALL operation can only be performed at minimum intervals of 5 minutes.

infoExport.title: Information
infoExport.content: You can download information as CSV or XLSX (Excel) files for better analysis by clicking the EXPORT button.

2_2_1_network.p3: Clicking the Statistical Information option will open a new window with the following information:
2_2_1_network.p4: Clicking the Gateway Information option will open a new window with the following information:
2_2_1_network.p5: Clicking on any node displayed in the topology allows you to view detailed information about the selected node.

2_2_1_device.title: 2.2.1 Device
2_2_1_device.p1: The Device page is useful for gathering information for individual analysis of network devices. A table is displayed to check network devices individually and to verify information such as Last Communication Date, LQI, RSSI, and other relevant information.

infoDisplay.title: Information
infoDisplay.content: You can view additional device parameters by clicking Display Setting.

2_2_1_device.p2: The Action column allows the user to perform two different operations on a specific device: Diagnose and Statistics.
2_2_1_device.diagnoseContent: This operation is useful when it is necessary to check the connectivity of each listed device individually. A Ping operation can be performed using the (Diagnose) button in the Action column of a specific device row. Clicking this button will display a small window:

warningDiagnose.title: Warning
warningDiagnose.content: A Diagnose is considered optimal status when it results in 0% Packet Loss.

2_2_1_device.statsContent: This operation is useful when it is necessary to check detailed information about a specific device. You can check information about geographic position, alarms, child nodes, and network quality measurements. Click the Statistics button in the Action column of a specific device row. Clicking this button will display the page:

controle-iluminacao.p1: This chapter details lighting control operations in the Streetlight system, including on/off and other functions.

3_1.title: 3.1 Turn Luminaires On/Off

precondition.title: Precondition
precondition.content: A smart lighting controller must be registered and communicating with the system.

executionItems: Go to: LESS > Monitor;
Select the desired smart controller;
Click [On/Off] to operate remotely.
Drag the vertical bar to set the dimming level.

3_2.title: 3.2 Other Control Functions

precondition.title: Precondition
precondition.content: A smart lighting controller must be registered and communicating with the system.

executionItems: Read Real Time Data
Position.

postcondition.title: Postcondition
postcondition.content: A success or failure notification will be displayed. On success, the luminaire status will be updated to off or on, as per the command.

4_1.title: 4.1 Device Manage
4_1.p1: This chapter describes the Device Center features in the Streetlight system, including organization, management, and firmware updates.

precondition.title: Precondition
precondition.content: Access to the Streetlight system with valid credentials.

4_1_1.title: 4.1.1 Organize List
4_1_1.p1: Organize and group street luminaires in different regions for decentralized control.
items: Go to: LESS > Device Center > Organize List;
Click on a node to display the public lighting equipment under it;
Click [Add Device] to display ungrouped devices, select them and assign them to the organizational node;
Click [Action] to remove the device grouping.

4_1_2.title: 4.1.2 Device Management
4_1_2.p1: Device management supports viewing lighting status, detailed device information, adding, importing and modifying basic device information, configuring and reading task execution modes, configuring and reading light thresholds, and configuring longitude, latitude and time zones.
4_1_2.instruction: Go to: LESS > Device Center > Device Manage to edit the group and device configuration.

4_1_2_1.title: 4.1.2.1 Running Mode Configuration
4_1_2_1.p1: Click [Running Mode] > [Set Running Mode/Read Running Mode] to set or read the controller's running mode.
4_1_2_1.note: Running mode configuration is only supported by controllers with a light sensor.

4_1_2_2.title: 4.1.2.2 Device Add and Remove Configuration
items: Click [Device Action] > Add to add a single device.
Click [Device Action] > Import to add a list of devices.
Click [Device Action] > Export to export the list of registered devices.
Click [Device Action] > Remove to remove a device.
Click [Device Action] > Edit Group to change the device group.

4_1_2_3.title: 4.1.2.3 Illumination Threshold Configuration
4_1_2_3.p1: Click [illumination Threshold] > [Set/Read illumination Threshold] to set or read the illumination threshold.
4_1_2_3.note: The illumination threshold defines the activation threshold for the lamp to turn on or off automatically, i.e., the critical luminosity point for on/off control of the lamp.

4_1_2_4.title: 4.1.2.4 Configure Device Information
4_1_2_4.p1: Click [Actions] to modify: Latitude, Longitude, Controller Information and Timezone.
4_1_2_4.warning: If it is necessary to resend the Timezone information, you can use the Retry Timezone button.

4_2.title: 4.2 Firmware Update
4_2.p1: Supports viewing firmware update status, updating packages and creating update records.
items: Click LESS > Device Center > Firmware Update
Select the ID and click UPGRADE

5_1.title: 5.1 Light Analysis
5_1.p1: Click [LESS] > [Analysis] > [Light Analysis] to view historical data.

5_2.title: 5.2 Lighting Analysis
5_2.p1: Click [LESS] > [Analysis] > [Lighting Analysis] to view the illumination rate analysis chart for the selected time period.
5_2.info: If you need to export the chart, the Download button is available.

6_1.title: 6.1 Strategy
6_1.p2: Click Add to add a new Strategy.
6_1.p3: Once created, you need to add Tasks to the created Strategy. Click on the created Strategy and then click Add to add a new Task.
6_1.p4: In the example above we have a strategy indicating the following intervals:
items: Between 18:30 and 02:00 > 100% illumination;
Between 02:00 and 06:00 > 80% illumination;
Between 06:00 and 18:30 > 0% illumination (OFF).

6_2.title: 6.2 Tasks
6_2.p2: Select a lighting controller and click the Add button to apply the task.

corte-religue.p1: Here we present the relay open/close (disconnect/reconnect) functionality. Before executing the command, it is important to know the current state of the module to be operated. Therefore, reading Appendix A - How to read the relay state is recommended.

7_1.title: 7.1 Disconnect

precondition.title: Precondition
precondition.content: At least one MM must have its relay closed or Connected.

executionItems: Open ORCA;
In the sidebar menu go to Operational Commands > Disconnect/Connect;
Select the meter and send the disconnection command.

postcondition.title: Postcondition
postcondition.content: A screen with the list of selected modules will appear showing the progress. On success, the message will return Disconnect Success. When reading the state, it will appear as Open or Disconnected.

7_2.title: 7.2 Reconnect

precondition.title: Precondition
precondition.content: At least one meter must have its relay Open or Disconnected.

executionItems: Open ORCA;
In the sidebar menu go to Operational Commands > Disconnect/Connect;
Select the protocol (e.g.: IDIS) and send the connection command.

postcondition.title: Postcondition
postcondition.content: On success, the message will return Connect Success. When reading the state, it will appear as Connected.

precondition.title: Precondition
precondition.content: Meter online and properly registered in MDC.

leitura-demanda.p1: On-demand reading requires selecting the correct protocol and the desired Data Item.
executionItems: Navigate to Operational Commands > On Demand Reading;
Select the appropriate Node in the asset tree;
Choose the Protocol Type;
Enter the Meter No. (or select from list);
Select the parameters you want to read (Energy, Voltage, Current, etc.);
Click Read or On Demand Reading.

9_1.title: 9.1 Update Date and Time

precondition.title: Precondition
precondition.content: At least one meter must be online and communicating with the system.

executionItems: Open ORCA and go to Operational Commands > Time Synchronization;
Select the meter protocol;
Select the meters or the box that will receive the command;
Click the Synchronizing Time button;
Choose between Server Clock (server time) or Customized Selection (manual time);
Click Ok and then Confirm to send the command.

postcondition.title: Postcondition
postcondition.content: A screen showing all selected modules and the operation result (Success/Failure) will be displayed.

10_1.title: 10.1 Read
10_1.p1: Verification of the current display configuration of the meter.
items: Select the meter and click the button to read what is being displayed on the screen;
The reading result should match what is physically shown on the display.

10_2.title: 10.2 Change Display
executionItems: Select the meter whose display will be changed;
Select the items to be shown on the display;
The order in which items are selected will be the order in which they are displayed in the automatic LCD screen rotation;
Confirm and send the configuration.

postcondition.title: Postcondition
postcondition.content: Physically check the equipment's LCD screen to confirm that the selected items are actually being displayed in the order they were configured.

parametrizacao.p1: For parameterization, we have flows for reading current parameters and sending new configurations.

11_1.title: 11.1 Read
11_1.p1: Allows reading the current parameters stored in the Terminal/Meter.

11_2.title: 11.2 Configuration
executionItems: In the sidebar menu go to: Configuration > Parameters Configuration > Meter Parameters;
Select the meter protocol (e.g.: IDIS);
A list of devices should appear; select the test device;
Select the parameterization category;
A configuration list will appear on the right (e.g.: selection of alarms to be activated);
Send the command.

postcondition.title: Postcondition
postcondition.content: A screen showing the operation success will be displayed.

tarifas.p1: The configuration of tariff models follows a strict creation flow (Daily, Weekly, Seasonal, Holiday) for subsequent application.

12_1.title: 12.1 Registering a Tariff Model
12_1.p1: First, you need to create a generic tariff model by going to Configuration > Parameters Configuration > Meter Tariff Definitions;
12_1.p2: Then, click the magnifying glass to configure the templates by period:

12_1_1.title: 12.1.1 Daily Template
items: Go to Configuration > Parameters Configuration > Meter Tariff;
Select Daily Template and click Add;
Create the time periods (Time Period List), schedules and applied rates (Tariff Rate);
Save the daily model.

12_1_2.title: 12.1.2 Weekly Template
items: Select Weekly Template and click Add;
Define the name of the weekly model;
For each day of the week, select the previously created Daily Template;
Save the operation.

12_1_3.title: 12.1.3 Seasonal Template
items: Select Seasonal Template and add a new one;
Set the start date and associate it with the created Weekly Template;
Save.

12_1_4.title: 12.1.4 Holiday Template (Common and Special)
items: Select Holiday and click Add in the Common or Special Holiday field;
Set the name, fixed (or recurring) date and apply the specific Daily Template for the holiday.

12_2.title: 12.2 Selecting a Tariff Model
12_2.p1: To apply the created model, select the desired meter and click the Current Tariff button or send the compiled tariff parameterization to the Node.

postcondition.title: Result
postcondition.content: The screen will display the result of the tariff parameterization request with success status.

relatorios.p1: This chapter presents the environment readings screen (MDC Reports).

13_1.title: 13.1 Readings

precondition.title: Precondition
precondition.content: At least one registered meter with a data push task configured and communicating correctly in the system.

executionItems: In the sidebar menu go to Reports > Readings;
Select the query period (Time/Date);
Select the node to be queried (Node);
Select the reading type (e.g.: Energy, Billing, Load Profile);
Click search/export.

alarmes.p1: Procedures for validation and consultation of events and alarms reported by the device to the system.
items: Access the Alarms/Events menu in ORCA;
Filter by the specific Terminal/Meter;
Trigger the alarm physically (e.g.: open cover, if applicable and safe) or simulate via command;
Verify receipt of the alarm packet in the system with the correct Timestamp.

15_1.title: 15.1 A - How to Read the Relay State
15_1.p1: Knowing the current relay state is crucial before sending on-demand reading operational commands;
items: Go to the on-demand reading operational commands screen;
Search for the Data Item referring to Relay Status / Disconnect Control;
Perform the reading;
Interpret the numerical/boolean result returned in the table (e.g.: 0 = Connected, 1 = Disconnected).
15_1.imageStatusRele: Print: Relay Status Data Item Reading
